Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 25-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIRST SEMESTER M.TECH. EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  High Performance Computing Systems [CSS_5103]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                        Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Evaluate the trade-offs between using parallel for and parallel sections. Develop a OpenMP                 (5)  
  program that uses reduction clause to calculate the dot product of two vectors of size N.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Illustrate how digital computers are classified in Flynn's classification along with their applications?   (3)  
  Also, mention on what basis they are classified  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Explain parallel processing ? Describe 3 types of concurrent events.                                       (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2)                Develop a MPI program to read a value M and N X M number of elements in the root. Using N                  (4)  
  processes do the following task. Find the square of first M numbers, find the cube of next M  
  A)           numbers and so on. Print the results in the root. Do not use any built-in math functions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
  B)           Implement the Odd-Even Transposition Sort algorithm for sorting N elements using a one-                    (3)  
  dimensional mesh processor array.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Analyze how MPI_Reduce() can be used to perform a global sum or maximum operation across all (3)  
  processes. Explain how reduction improves performance compared to local computation and  
  communication.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                What is Command queue ? Illustrate the OpenCL steps required to transfer data from the host to             (5)  
  the device, execute a kernel, and retrieve the result.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Construct an OpenCL kernel for multiplying two matrices A and B of size M X N and N X P. Each              (3)  
  row of A has to be multiplied by a separate work item.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  Page #1

C)         Determine how OpenCL can be used to implement a program that utilizes both CPU and GPU for             (2)  
  parallel computation. Explain how this heterogeneous execution impacts the performance of the  
  application  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Construct a parallel algorithm to sum n values using the Hypercube SIMD model, where n is the          (4)  
  total number of values to be added and p is the number of processors.  
  A)         Assume that each processor initially holds one of the n values.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Illustrate the working of a Distributed Memory architecture in the multiprocessor by describing how    (3)  
  data is shared among processors.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Discuss the taxonomy and classification of static and dynamic interconnection networks used in         (3)  
  parallel computer architectures.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO6" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5)              Develop a CUDA program to read a matrix of size 3 × 3. The kernel you write should meet the            (4)  
  following specifications:  
  A)  
  With respect to each row in the matrix, find first element to the power of 2, second element to the  
  power of 3, third element to the power of 4. An example data is shown in Fig. Q 5A. You need to  
  use number of CUDA threads as number of rows of matrix to make this task feasible.  
  
  $$Matrix A =$$  
  1 2 3  
  4 3 2  
  3 2 2  
  
  $$Matrix B =$$  
  1 8 81  
  16 27 16  
  9 8 16  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
  B)         Demonstrate various types of CUDA program variables and their memory types, scope and lifetime. (3)  
  What happens when we use __host__ and __device__ in a function declaration?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Develop a CUDA kernel for matrix multiplication in which each block computes one row of the            (3)  
  resultant matrix  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
  
  -----End-----
